title: Embedding behavioural and implementation science in a whole school approach to promote physical activity among children and young people with disabilities
content:
by Erin Byrd, Jason J. Wilson, Paul McFlynn, Victoria Simms, Laurence Taggart, Áine Boner, Marie H. Murphy

Background

A whole school approach (WSA) to physical activity is a comprehensive strategy encouraging children's physical activity throughout the school day. However, research on implementing this approach in special educational needs (SEN) school settings is limited. A strategic approach that considers the school context, behaviour change mechanisms and implementation strategies can improve the effectiveness and sustainability of physical activity in a WSA. This study aimed to embed implementation and behavioural science principles to co-develop an implementation research logic model (IRLM) to guide implementation of a WSA to physical activity in SEN settings.

Methods

A collaborative co-development approach was used in this study exploring the WSA to physical activity in SEN settings. Teachers, school leadership, parents, the education authority and professionals from community sports clubs in one UK region participated in a series of workshops. The workshops and analyses were guided by behavioural and implementation theories, models, and frameworks.

Results

Workshop discussions revealed 31 determinants of implementation, comprising 18 facilitators, 12 barriers and one item identified as both barrier and facilitator. These determinants informed the development of eight implementation strategies to promote physical activity through a WSA in SEN settings (e.g., staff training, building collaborative networks and engaging families). Eleven implementation, seven school-level and six pupil-level outcomes, were identified to assess effectiveness and implementation. Eight causal mechanisms explained the pathway from strategies to outcomes. Finally, these determinants, implementation strategies, mechanisms, and outcomes were mapped onto an IRLM to guide the implementation of a WSA to physical activity for children and young people with SENs across settings.

Conclusions

We have co-developed an IRLM embedded in implementation and behavioural science to support the implementation of a WSA to physical activity in SEN settings. The model illustrates causal mechanisms between implementation determinants and implementation strategies to achieve intended outcomes. This IRLM has informed a guidance document for implementing WSA to physical activity within SEN settings, addressing real-world challenges faced in promoting physical activity among pupils with SEN.
